cases.question: Our app repeatedly fetches the same JSON. How do ETag and If-None-Match avoid downloading an unchanged body, and can an ETag also eliminate the request? Explain the ordinary successful GET case. Keep all seven claims and useful qualifications; maximum 170 words.
cases.original:
Use an ETag to let the client check whether its stored response can be reused. The server sends an ETag with the JSON response, and a later conditional GET includes that value in If-None-Match. If the tag matches the selected representation, the server returns 304 Not Modified without a response body, allowing the client to reuse its stored body. If it does not match, a successful GET returns 200 OK with the current JSON.

This validation still involves a request. To permit reuse without validation, configure an appropriate freshness policy, such as Cache-Control: max-age=60, subject to the other caching rules. The cached response can then be reused while fresh; this does not promise that the underlying data will remain unchanged for 60 seconds.
claims: DTC1: ETag enables stored-response validation. Strength: recommendation_supported_by_specification. Scope: Stored response; GET.
DTC2: Server supplies the ETag; client echoes it in If-None-Match. Strength: mechanism. Scope: Described conditional GET.
DTC3: A matching tag produces 304, no body, and stored-body reuse. Strength: conditional_requirement. Scope: Selected representation; otherwise successful GET.
DTC4: A nonmatching tag permits 200 with current JSON. Strength: conditional_behavior. Scope: Successful GET, not every possible response.
DTC5: Validation still sends a request. Strength: categorical_within_scope. Scope: Described conditional validation.
DTC6: Freshness can permit reuse without validation; max-age=60 is illustrative. Strength: qualified_recommendation. Scope: Other caching rules apply.
DTC7: Fresh reuse does not guarantee unchanged origin data for 60 seconds. Strength: permission_and_non_guarantee. Scope: Illustrative freshness interval.

cases.original:
How to use Anti-Detection Writing Skill on your next draft

An AI draft can be accurate and still take too long to get to the point. Anti-Detection Writing Skill gives your agent a repeatable editing process: identify what the reader needs, preserve the facts, improve the flow, and review the result. You can also request a measured comparison with GPTZero.


Start with one reply, email, or section of documentation.


1. Install the skill.


npx skills add dexhunter/anti-detection-writing-skill --skill anti-detection-writing


Choose your agent in the installer. The default installation is for the current project.


2. Supply the context and original text.


Tell the agent who will read it and what they need to do. For a technical reply, include the question, relevant documentation, and any version constraints. Then ask:


“Use $anti-detection-writing to make this text smoother and easier to read for [audience]. Preserve its facts, code, and qualifications. Remove repetition and irrelevant background. Explain any factual corrections, and get a separate review of the final text.”


The useful edit might move a prerequisite before an instruction, replace an ambiguous pronoun, or cut a repeated explanation. Keep checking that the advice still means the same thing.


3. Measure a detector result if you need one.


“Compare the original and final text using GPTZero Basic Scan. Use the same displayed model and record the exact inputs, all three confidences, dates, and warnings. Keep unchanged and worse results too.”


Live scanning needs your own detector access and a browser tool your agent supports. The skill does not supply either. Review correctness and readability separately from the score.


What the development examples show


A fresh recheck of one saved Qwen Code reply returned 100% AI / 0% mixed / 0% human → 1% AI / 99% mixed / 0% human in GPTZero Basic Scan, Model 4.9b, on September 6, 2026. The screenshots show those completed scans. This repeats a development case; it is not a new test of the packaged skill.


The change was a short, relevant quotation from the asker added to an otherwise identical answer. This comparison changed both content and length; it does not show a benefit from rewriting alone. A 99% mixed result does not mean 99% human.


Across the development sample, 5 of 10 quotation comparisons reduced AI confidence; plain rewriting reduced it in 0 of 15 comparisons. Separate LLM reviewers rated eight plain revisions clearer and seven equivalent. The observations came from completed UI scans, and the current packaged skill has not yet been prospectively validated for detector performance.


Use a quotation when it helps answer the question. Keep a clear, correct edit even if the detector outcome is unchanged, subject to your publication requirements.


Try it on one draft, then share what improved or fell short in Discussions. The repository includes exact inputs, measured examples, and the unsuccessful cases.


Repository: https://github.com/dexhunter/anti-detection-writing-skill


Discussions: https://github.com/dexhunter/anti-detection-writing-skill/discussions


Before: plain answer, 100% AI / 0% mixed / 0% human. After: the same answer plus one relevant asker quotation, 1% AI / 99% mixed / 0% human. GPTZero Basic Scan, Model 4.9b; fresh recheck on September 6, 2026. These genuine screenshots show the result panels and part of each input; the complete inputs are linked in the repository. Adding a quotation changes content and length.
claims: AX1: The skill offers repeatable editing to identify reader needs, preserve facts, improve flow and review; detector comparison is optional, without a success guarantee.
AX2: A reader can start with one reply, email or documentation section; editing and measurement are separate tasks.
AX3: Install with the exact npx command; choose the agent in the installer; the default scope is the current project.
AX4: Supply the original text, intended audience and purpose. Technical replies also need their question, relevant documentation and version constraints.

AX5: The example editing request asks for smoother readable prose, preservation of facts/code/qualifications, removal of repetition and irrelevant background, explanations of factual corrections and separate review of exact final text.
AX6: Useful edits may move prerequisites, clarify pronouns or remove repeated explanations, while preserving the meaning of the advice.

AX7: Optional comparison uses original and final prose separately from code in GPTZero Basic Scan with the same displayed model; save exact inputs, all three confidences, dates, warnings, unchanged and worse results. Code/full-message correctness is reviewed separately. This supersedes the earlier source example's full-text instruction under the user's latest scope request.
AX8: Live scanning needs the user's own detector access and an agent-supported browser tool. The skill supplies neither. Review correctness/readability separately from score.
AX9: A saved Qwen Code reply pair was freshly rechecked September 6, 2026 using GPTZero Basic Scan Model 4.9b: before AI100/Mixed0/Human0; after AI1/Mixed99/Human0.
AX10: The existing screenshots show that completed Qwen recheck, not this article or a new prospective test of the packaged skill.
AX11: The measured change added one short relevant asker quotation while the answer body stayed identical. Content and length both changed; it does not isolate a rewriting benefit.
AX12: 99% mixed does not mean 99% human and lower confidence does not establish human authorship.

AX13: In the dated development sample, 5 of 10 quotation comparisons reduced AI confidence, while 0 of 15 plain-rewrite comparisons did. These are development-sample counts, not all subsequent research.
AX14: Separate LLM reviewers rated eight plain revisions clearer and seven equivalent; this is not a human preference study.
AX15: Observations are completed UI scans; the current packaged skill has not been prospectively validated for reliable detector performance.
AX16: Include a quotation only when it helps answer the question. A correct clear edit can remain useful with an unchanged score, subject to the user's publication requirements.
AX17: Readers can try a draft and share improvements or failures in Discussions. The repository contains exact inputs, measured examples and unsuccessful cases; preserve both destination URLs.

AX18: Preserve a caption for the two genuine before/after screenshots: same Qwen body plus quotation, native confidence triplets, Basic Scan Model 4.9b, September 6 recheck, visible panels plus partial input, full inputs linked in repository, content/length change. No screenshot score is attributed to the article.
